title: Japan's 'Donald McDonald' Officially Becomes 'Ronald'
paragraphs: McDonald's has a famous clown mascot named Ronald McDonald. But in Japan, he has had a different name for more than 50 years. Now, that is changing.

On October 1, McDonald's Japan surprised many people with a message on its official X account. In the message, the mascot said, "From today, I'm Ronald." This means the character in Japan now has the same name as in other countries.

Ronald McDonald first appeared in TV commercials in the US in 1963. When the first McDonald's restaurant opened in Japan in 1971, the mascot was given the name "Donald McDonald." Since then, people in Japan have known him as Donald.

Nobody is completely sure why his name was different. One popular idea is that the founder of McDonald's Japan, Den Fujita, thought "Ronald" would be hard for Japanese people to say. Another idea is that the company wanted to avoid confusion with Ranald MacDonald, a man who became the first native English speaker to teach English in Japan in 1848.

The mascot is not the only thing with a new name. On the same day, the charity Donald McDonald House in Japan also changed its name to Ronald McDonald House. The charity supports sick children and their families. It said its name and logo would change, but its work would stay the same.

People in Japan had many different reactions to the news online. Some said it was the biggest shock of the year. Others joked that the name a person uses for the mascot shows how old they are. Some people said they would continue to call him Donald, while others said it would take some time to get used to the new name.
